prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

New part:
S189: The Tower Supervisor verifies that any proposed reduction in declared runway use is consistent with observed traffic, controller workload, and the current safety position.
S190: The Airport Duty Manager verifies that airfield operations checks have been completed before requesting changes to Airport Acceptance Rate values or departure metering assumptions.
S191: The Regional Flow Platform receives confirmed capacity impacts through normal system interfaces after local duty coordination has established the airport position.
S192: The Capacity Assessment Module may use the confirmed airport position to recalculate available capacity, but it does not originate local airfield safety judgments.
S193: The Alert Distribution Hub distributes approved duty coordination alerts to affected operational roles when a local condition changes runway availability, taxi routing, or apron access.
S194: The Identity Access Service restricts entry of duty desk confirmations to authorized airport operations staff and records each transaction in the Audit Event Ledger.
S195: If the Airport CDM Portal is unavailable, the Contingency Operations Console provides a degraded channel for recording tower and duty desk decisions until normal service is restored.
S196: During shift handover, the outgoing Airport Duty Manager briefs open safety checks, unresolved surveillance discrepancies, and any tower coordination points that remain active.
S197: After operations, the Performance Analytics Warehouse compares recorded duty coordination events with actual movement data to identify delays, missed checks, and opportunities to improve local decision quality.
S198: This section defines how apron movement management is executed after the Airport Duty Manager handover has identified active surface constraints.
S199: In ramp operations, Ramp Control Lead is also called Quartzline during voice and chat coordination.
S200: The Ramp Control Lead maintains the operational sequence for pushbacks, stand exits, stand entries, and towing movements within the controlled apron area.
S201: Pushback sequencing is based on safety separation, published stand constraints, crew readiness, ground handling completion, and the relationship between Target Off Block Time and Calculated Takeoff Time.
S202: The Ramp Control Lead shall not release a pushback until the Tower Supervisor has confirmed that the movement can be integrated with the active ground route and runway plan.
S203: The Ramp Movement Board is the primary working view for planned apron movements, active conflicts, towing tasks, and occupied stand intervals.
S204: Surface Surveillance Adapter inputs support the Ramp Control Lead by confirming aircraft position, stand occupancy, and blocking conditions on critical apron lanes.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
